Works with

Rugged tablet for Idhammar MMS

Idhammar MMS is the maintenance management system (CMMS) and OEE platform from Idhammar Systems Limited, a UK software company based in London SW19 which says it has supplied CMMS and OEE systems since 1971. Its customer list is heavy on UK food and drink manufacturing (the vendor names Unilever, Premier Foods, Hovis, 2 Sisters, Aunt Bessies, Aspall and Chivers Brothers), and a sector edition called Idhammar Response is sold to emergency services, including fire and rescue. The mobile side is Idhammar Connect, an Android app released on Google Play on 3 October 2023 that lets technicians, stores staff and station personnel handle work orders, inspections, defect reports and inventory checks away from a desk.

On the plant floor or in a fire station workshop that means carrying a device between lines, plant rooms and stores, often with gloves on, near wash-down areas and sometimes where Wi-Fi is poor. A consumer tablet usually has no ingress or drop rating, so it needs a case and careful handling in those conditions. A rugged Android tablet is the usual answer, provided it meets the app's published requirements.

This page sets out what Idhammar Systems publishes about running Idhammar Connect, matches those requirements to the Tuga A10, Tuga A8 and Tuga A6, and covers setup, accessories and the questions buyers usually ask. Where the vendor publishes nothing (screen size, NFC, Windows), we say so rather than guess.

Requirements

What Idhammar MMS (with the Idhammar Connect mobile app) needs from a device

Each item below comes from Idhammar Systems Limited's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android device running Android 5.0 or later

    Idhammar Connect (package com.idhammar.connect) is published on Google Play by a developer shown as Idhammar MMS; the About the developer panel names IDHAMMAR SYSTEMS LIMITED at Dalton House, 60 Windsor Avenue, London SW19 2RR. The listing's app data gives a minimum of Android 5.0 and up (API level 21), with the current version 9.0.1 updated on 6 August 2026 and 100+ downloads. Check the Requires Android line in the App info panel of the live listing before you order a fleet. Source: play.google.com

  • No iOS or Windows app found; some features may stay on the desktop

    The vendor's launch post (31 October 2023) calls Idhammar Connect its Android app and says users work directly from their Android devices. The same post says that some features might still be exclusive to the desktop version, at least in the initial phases. Apple's App Store search for the GB and US storefronts returned no Idhammar app, and a Microsoft Store search for the GB market returned no Idhammar products. Idhammar Systems publishes no Windows, browser or hardware requirements for the desktop system. Source: idhammarsystems.com

  • Offline working with automatic sync when reconnected

    The vendor's blog post of 27 March 2025 states that having no internet is not problematic, that teams can work offline with Idhammar Connect, and that it syncs automatically once back online. The Google Play description itself does not mention offline use, so this rests on the vendor's blog rather than the store listing. Source: idhammarsystems.com

  • Barcode and QR code scanning on parts and assets

    The vendor's blog post of 27 March 2025 says barcode and QR code scanning speeds up identifying the correct part or equipment, and presents Idhammar Connect as its app for this way of working. A December 2023 post says mobile devices can be used to scan barcodes to identify assets and that their in-built cameras can be used to attach images to work orders. The vendor does not say how scanning is done, publishes no dedicated scanner requirement and no list of supported scanners, so plan on camera-based scanning and confirm with Idhammar Systems. Source: idhammarsystems.com

  • NFC and RFID: not a published feature

    A search of the vendor site for NFC returns no results, and NFC does not appear in the Google Play listing. RFID appears once, in a November 2022 blog post as a general industry comment about asset tracking devices, not as an Idhammar Connect feature. Do not buy on the assumption that NFC or RFID tagging works with the app. Source: idhammarsystems.com

  • Mobile use where Wi-Fi signal may be poor, with a camera for photos and files

    The vendor's emergency services page says Idhammar Connect gives firefighters access via mobile devices to report defects on the move and perform inspections and inventories on the station forecourt where Wi-Fi signal may be poor. The sectors page says station staff record station tests and inventory checks via a mobile device and that checks performed at the fireground are synchronised on return to the station. The Google Play data safety section says the app may collect photos and videos and files and docs, and that data is encrypted in transit, so expect technicians to use the camera for attachments. Source: idhammarsystems.com

Worth knowing. Idhammar Connect is published as an Android app. We found no iOS app and no Windows app or Microsoft Store listing, and Idhammar Systems publishes no Windows or browser requirements for the desktop system, so we do not recommend the Windows-based Tuga W10 for this app. The vendor also says that some features might still be exclusive to the desktop version, so technicians may still need a PC for some tasks. The vendor does not say how barcode and QR scanning is done; the Tuga A10 has no dedicated scan engine, and while the A6 has an integrated 2D barcode scanner, the vendor publishes no supported-scanner list, so plan on camera-based scanning and treat the A6's scanner as something to test. NFC and RFID are not published Idhammar Connect features, so do not buy either device for that purpose.
Setting up

Getting Idhammar MMS (with the Idhammar Connect mobile app) running

  1. Idhammar Connect is the vendor's mobile app for the Idhammar MMS system, so arrange user accounts for your technicians with Idhammar Systems or your Idhammar administrator before the devices arrive.
  2. On the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, sign in to Google Play and install Idhammar Connect (package com.idhammar.connect, developer shown as Idhammar MMS).
  3. Open the app and sign in with the credentials your Idhammar administrator provides.
  4. Before taking devices to areas with poor signal, confirm with your administrator how offline working and automatic sync are configured for your system, and test a sync on return to Wi-Fi or mobile signal.
  5. Grant the app camera and storage permissions when prompted so that barcode or QR scanning and photo attachments work.
  6. Fit the A10 to the charging dock or vehicle mounting dock, or clip the A6 into a belt holster, and set a charging routine at shift end.
